scope: Native MuJoCo diagnostic with production RTNeural and math headers, explicitly transcribed ROS activation plumbing; not a ROS execution or hardware approval.
controller_fix: Initialization and fade start at the selected trick clip first joint pose. Network normalization/action defaults remain fixed; effective pre-clamp action goes into history. Ordinary walking/default-pose activation arithmetic is preserved; unknown clips and invalid anchors refuse activation.
sequence: Standing -> Spider entry(0.5s init+1s fade+7.6s clip+0.3s) -> walking(2s init+2s fade+0.2s) -> forward0.10m/s2s -> stop1s -> backward0.10m/s2s -> yaw0.20rad/s2s -> stop2s -> selected Spider exit(0.5s init+1s fade+7.6s clip+0.3s) -> standing hold1s. Physical position/velocity and16ms target-delay buffer persist through all switches; activation resets controller observations and phase only.
interpretation: All 8 bounded sequences completed without reaching the configured1.5rad tilt stop, with zero physical resets and unchanged watched sources. This is completion evidence, not an invented safe/unsafe score.

Legacy exit activation creates an unintended stand/drop excursion before playing the low-stance exit reference. Selected-clip anchoring removes that excursion under both contact models and both command-limit variants.

In torso-only+class-driver comparison, maximum fade tilt drops37.75 degrees to0.65 degrees; full-hull+class-driver drops11.51 degrees to2.82 degrees. Exit playback itself still reaches9.33 degrees with full hulls/class driver.
Fixed-activation forward speed averages 0.041–0.064m/s for a0.10m/s request over only 2 s. This short transition diagnostic does not validate the complete walking speed range.

Both worlds retain their chosen geometry for the whole sequence. Full-hull world includes additional leg-ground support that the walking policy was not trained with; torso-only world omits leg hull contacts used by the tracking policy. Neither mismatch is hidden by swapping models or resetting between phases.
limitations: Native CPU solver at520Hz differs from250Hz training Warp solver.
Nominal model: no observation noise, IMU delay, encoder bias, parameter randomization or external push.
Clip completion is controller clock/status, not measured joint settlement; endpoint errors reported separately.
No final walking-controller activation after standing exit; bounded diagnostic stops in trick standing hold.
Only one deterministic nominal world per variant; no timing jitter, stale command handling, ROS controller-manager process, hardware safety circuit or actuator temperature validation.
Ground contacts are compliant MuJoCo constraints; minimum distances are penetration diagnostics, not hard no-penetration guarantees.
The locally supplied class driver bounds are not verified as the installed robot bounds.
